newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil drifts in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil drifts in quiet trade.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps drifted sideways in quiet trade late afternoon on Wednesday with no clear direction seen from the physical market where support from local traders at current levels are expected for the rest of the month, traders said.
"The market is going nowhere, it's pretty quiet this afternoon," one broker said.
May gas oil swaps were last quoted at $25.60/$25.70 per barrel, down from Tuesday's $25.80/$25.90.
June gas oil also fell to $24.25/$24.35 per barrel, down from $24.45/$24.55. June traded earlier in the day at $24.32.
The falls mirrored the overnight June Brent crude fall of 35 cents to close at $17.99 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange but rebounded slightly on Wednesday to last trade at $18.19.
Traders said the market is expected to be well supported for the rest of the month by afew traders who have bought close to 15 million barrels of physical gas oil since early March.
The traders on Tuesday bought four 150,000-barrel cargoes at between $26.60 to $27.50 for early to second half May loading.
Others said the market was also looking to large purchases from India for June arrival diesel for support. India on Wednesday issued a tender to buy 0.25 percent and 1.0 percent diesel.

India bought an unexpectedly large 870,000 tonnes of diesel for May delivery which helped absorb some of the more than 1.6 million tonnes of arbitrage cargoes that were shipped to this region from the West.
The fuel oil swaps also fell slightly with the lower crude values with May last quoted at $97.75/$98.75 per tonne, from $98.00/$98.50 on Tuesday.
